nano-01-c2.text: U.S. National Science Foundation (2023). NSF congratulates laureates of the 2023 Nobel Prize in chemistry. NSF News.
nano-01-c2.quote: for the discovery and synthesis of quantum dot technology.
nano-01-c2.claim: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Bawendi, Brus, and Ekimov for discovering and synthesizing these nanocrystals.

nano-02-c3.text: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (1996). The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1996 (Press release). NobelPrize.org.
nano-02-c3.quote: New forms of the element carbon – called fullerenes – in which the atoms are arranged in closed shells was discovered in 1985 by Robert F. Curl, Harold W. Kroto and Richard E. Smalley.
nano-02-c3.claim: was discovered by Kroto, Curl, and Smalley in 1985 (Nobel 1996)

nano-03-c1.text: Radisavljevic B, Radenovic A, Brivio J, Giacometti V, Kis A (2011). Single-layer MoS2 transistors. Nature nanotechnology.
nano-03-c1.quote: demonstrate transistors with room-temperature current on/off ratios of 1 × 10(8) and ultralow standby power dissipation.
nano-03-c1.claim: in 2011 Kis's group at EPFL demonstrated single-layer MoS₂ FETs with on/off ratios above 10⁸

nano-03-c3.text: Yuan Cao, Valla Fatemi, Shiang Fang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Efthimios Kaxiras, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero (2018). Magic-angle graphene superlattices: a new platform for unconventional superconductivity. arXiv.
nano-03-c3.quote: Here we report on the realization of intrinsic unconventional superconductivity in a 2D superlattice created by stacking two graphene sheets with a small twist angle.
nano-03-c3.claim: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (Cao, Jarillo-Herrero, 2018): rotate two graphene layers by 1.1° and a flat band emerges, hosting unconventional superconductivity at 1.7 K and correlated insulator phases.

nano-09-c1.text: Nobel Foundation (1986). The Nobel Prize in Physics 1986. NobelPrize.org.
nano-09-c1.quote: the other half jointly to Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer "for their design of the scanning tunneling microscope"
nano-09-c1.claim: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM), invented by Binnig and Rohrer at IBM Zurich in 1981 (Nobel 1986)
